searchText: late to discussion around the 0x02 proposal, had a couple minor questions <@!784446040073175040> : - this is only different from the 0x01 commitment w.r.t. priority fees right? not block/attestation/other consensus committee rewards - for priority fees, this would obviate the need for a 'withdrawal' process to translate from beacon chain -> eth1, right? Hello Lakshman! (also fwiw think that the decreased surface area for attacks on validators argument is really compelling) Yes, this is only different to 0x01 with respect to priority fees Those priority fees would stay on eth1 the whole time, no need to send them to eth2 - we originally thought this was the best idea but Mikhail said it would be very hard to do technically because it would add a synchronization constraint between the execution and consensus layers hmm ya, that's a good point i think generally effort has been made to reduce assumptions around sequentiality/linearity of the two systems Yeah that's my understanding as well Perhaps the security aspect makes it worth revisiting the idea for 0x01 instead of having separate credentials, though I am still hesitant because people are using 0x01 on mainnet today and we don't want to cause problems for them did past discussion about synchronization happen in a public channel somewhere? have been off for a week or so so playing catchup 🙂 Yeah it was in <#692062809701482577> before we made 0x02 a thing, I'll find it https://discordapp.com/channels/595666850260713488/692062809701482577/847503652653498368 Here it is Leaving decentralized staking injured at the feet of centralized staking is sure to result in centralized staking killing decentralized staking. The point of staking is to secure the network, but the result of rewarding something as easy as staking is that more than necessary will be staked. If decentralized staking is reserved for individuals with 6 figure USD, the masses will pool their money and animate a demagogue. Ethereum consensus can EASILY become centralized because the VAST MAJORITY of eth is held in small chunks. If the best option for this majority is to stake with centralized entities, the masses WILL unfortunately animate a demagogue. Decentralized pooling is injured at the feet of a looming and materializing phantom. 0x02 is important Case in point☝️ <@301186049323958275> I think that the counter arguments on the last eth2 call are valid — (1) this only targets coinbase fees on top of the 1559 burn (other MEV has no restriction to go to coinbase) and (2) it just encourages side channels for tx fees and non-coinbase use of mev In the honest case, it looks like a benefit, but in the honest case, you don’t need enforcement anyway. In the dishonest case, it encourages side-channel payments/markets and further obfuscates what’s going on I’m not saying there isn’t a problem for certain validator setups, but I’m not convinced that 0x02 is a solution Pretty much any TX and MEV value on top of the 1559 burn is subject to side-channel / non-coinbase payments *no matter what* you put into the base protocol even if fees were paid to the validator account itself, you still have this issue. All extractable value from the block can go to the producer of the block through any myriad of channels Another way to look at this is via the eth2.0 design goals: 1. Simplicity: minimize complexity, even at the cost of some losses in efficiency 0x02 proposal removes a hidden/underivable feature (that the “withdrawal” address isn’t always *the* withdrawal address). Sure, side-channels will still exist, but a complexity is still reduced. 2. Resilience: remain live through major network partitions and when very large portions of nodes go offline 0x02 or adding the functionality to 0x01 doesn’t violate this 3. Longevity: select all components such that they are either quantum secure or can be easily swapped out for quantum secure counterparts when available 0x02 or adding the functionality to 0x01 doesn’t violate this 4. Security: utilize crypto and design techniques that allow for a large participation of validators in total and per unit time This type of security might be provided by the security one gets with less avenues to hijack their coinbase payments without them knowing 5. Decentralization: allow for a typical consumer laptop with O(C) resources to process/validate O(1) shards (including any system level validation such as the beacon chain) 0x02 promotes more decentralized validators (maybe this is opinion) or at least discourages low eth stakers from going for the easy centralized route that also offers higher returns As for (1), this introduces consensus complexity whereas it is unclear if it solves the problem I'm worried it creates a *false* sense of security People who are going to hog all MEV/priority fees possible would do it regardless of 0x02 or not. This doesn't create an "extra" incentive. All it does is create additional work required for them to do it (and benefit from other peoples' staked eth) in order to do so. If in the dishonest case it prevents >0% of the dishonest actors from acting due to the increased complexity of setting up a side-channel vs a simple coinbase address change then I think it's worth it. especially for the MEV component of fees which has *zero* requirement to go to COINBASE It has zero requirement but the general (commonplace) mechanism that most node operators will use will depend on the "preconfigured"/default configurations provided. The question then becomes how easy <-> complex is it to deviate from this default mechanism main argument that made sense to me is that if a honest validator gets hacked, the hacker often wont bother to (or even know how to) modify it and establish a sidechannel for MEV esp if hacker is not crypto-targeted I think this is a valid concern but isn't really a reason to *not* do it. Does it add security vs not having it (especially w.r.t. the general security risk of a hacker surreptitiously changing a coinbase address)? Yes. Can it create a false sense of security? Potentially, which is why this (what 0x02 does and how it works, and what it doesn't do) should be clearly documented and explained.

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
I think that the counter arguments on the last eth2 call are valid — (1) this only targets coinbase fees on top of the 1559 burn (other MEV has no restriction to go to coinbase) and (2) it just encourages side channels for tx fees and non-coinbase use of mev

In the honest case, it looks like a benefit, but in the honest case, you don’t need enforcement anyway. In the dishonest case, it encourages side-channel payments/markets and further obfuscates what’s going on

I’m not saying there isn’t a problem for certain validator setups, but I’m not convinced that 0x02 is a solution

Pretty much any TX and MEV value on top of the 1559 burn is subject to side-channel / non-coinbase payments *no matter what* you put into the base protocol

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: even if fees were paid to the validator account itself, you still have this issue. All extractable value from the block can go to the producer of the block through any myriad of channels

excerpts.author: drdoofus0000
excerpts.content:
Another way to look at this is via the eth2.0 design goals:

1. Simplicity: minimize complexity, even at the cost of some losses in efficiency

    0x02 proposal removes a hidden/underivable feature (that the “withdrawal” address isn’t always *the* withdrawal address). Sure, side-channels will still exist, but a complexity is still reduced.

2. Resilience: remain live through major network partitions and when very large portions of nodes go offline

    0x02 or adding the functionality to 0x01 doesn’t violate this

3. Longevity: select all components such that they are either quantum secure or can be easily swapped out for quantum secure counterparts when available

    0x02 or adding the functionality to 0x01 doesn’t violate this

4. Security: utilize crypto and design techniques that allow for a large participation of validators in total and per unit time

    This type of security might be provided by the security one gets with less avenues to hijack their coinbase payments without them knowing

5. Decentralization: allow for a typical consumer laptop with O(C) resources to process/validate O(1) shards (including any system level validation such as the beacon chain)

    0x02 promotes more decentralized validators (maybe this is opinion) or at least discourages low eth stakers from going for the easy centralized route that also offers higher returns

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: As for (1), this introduces consensus complexity whereas it is unclear if it solves the problem

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: I'm worried it creates a *false* sense of security

If in the dishonest case it prevents >0% of the dishonest actors from acting due to the increased complexity of setting up a side-channel vs a simple coinbase address change then I think it's worth it.
